descripcion_geo: Region east of the Gulf of Aqaba, in present-day Saudi Arabia. Land of the descendants of Midian, son of Abraham and Keturah.
importancia_estrategica: Caravan passage land between Arabia and Egypt; place of the call of Moses.

historias.titulo: Moses in Midian and the burning bush
historias.descripcion: Moses flees from Egypt to Midian, marries Zipporah daughter of Jethro, and receives God's revelation at the burning bush.
Moses helps the daughters of the priest of Midian at the well and is invited to stay; He takes Zipporah as his wife.
The Midianites oppress Israel for seven years; Gideon with 300 men defeats the Midianite army.

personajes.descripcion: Father-in-law of Moses; He taught Moses to delegate judgment to the people.
Daughter of Jethro wife of Moses and mother of his children.
He liberated Israel from Midianite oppression with 300 men and torches in jars.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Land of shepherds and caravans where Moses found God in the burning bush; The priest Jethro worshiped the Most High God.

mitos.nombre: The bush that burns without being consumed

judaismo.descripcion: Moses sees the burning bush in Midian: God reveals himself as the 'I am that I am' (Ex 3:14).
judaismo.significado_teologico: Moses sees the burning bush in Midian: God reveals himself as the 'I am that I am' (Ex 3:14).

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: The burning bush is a symbol of the presence of God who reveals himself without consuming what he touches.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The burning bush is a symbol of the presence of God who reveals himself without consuming what he touches.

islam.descripcion: Moses (Musa) is a major prophet in Islam; His calling in Sinai/Midian is mentioned in the Qur'an (Cor 28:29-35).
islam.significado_teologico: Moses (Musa) is a major prophet in Islam; His calling in Sinai/Midian is mentioned in the Qur'an (Cor 28:29-35).
